text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Church of Central Africa Presbytery in Rumphi, northern Malawi, an opposition AFORD's (Alliance for Democracy) stronghold, is battling against moves to evict its reverend Chande Mhone on allegations that he supports the ruling United Democratic Front party.

- Wage dispute talks between government and civil servants have been halted as government team intends to consult cabinet after the workers' union demands that salaries be implemented in full, Malawi Congress of Trade Union Secretary general Francis Antonio said on Tuesday.
- Malawi which already has diplomatic ties with Isreal, is processing documents to establish ties with the Palestinian Authority, deputy director for political affairs Harry Mononga said on Tuesday.
- Malawi police have admitted there is a highly organised and sophisticated syndicate of criminals operating in the country almost at will and it cannot be brought before the courts of law.
- A Lilongwe Magistrate had to travel 300km to Blantyre to hear a bail application for three people after Blantyre magistrates shunned the 38 million kwacha ($2.5 million) bank fraud case.

- A prominent Blantyre township businessman who on Tuesday admitted beating up a colleague after an aborted business deal "to teach him a lesson" has earned the backing of Police Chief Patrick Chikapa.

- The appeal case against former President Kamuzu Banda on charges of plotting to murder three cabinet ministers and one member of parliament in 1983, scheduled for June 5, has been postponed to June 30, because the main defence lawyer, Clive Stanbrook is unble to arrive in Malawi before June 20.
